meta.description: How NVIDIA NIM picks a profile and how the NIM Profile Advisor reproduces it. Rules marked 'advisor' are this tool's own conventions for cases the NVIDIA docs do not cover.

selection_preference_order.rule: NIM evaluates a priority chain at start-up: NIM_MODEL_PROFILE=default (intelligent default: hardware compatibility, then backend priority, then LoRA configuration) > NIM_MODEL_PROFILE=<64-hex id or description> (exact profile) > memory-aware automatic selection > manifest selector (profile_selection_criteria, based on GPU device, VRAM and parallelism).
Automatic selection prefers profiles estimated to fit the available GPU memory and prefers non-LoRA profiles unless LoRA is enabled.

Prefer a direct gpu_device match over a tested_gpu_devices match, and either over a GPU-agnostic profile. Keep the fallbacks until the VRAM and GPU-count checks are done so a usable generic profile is not discarded early.
Inside the preferred tier choose lower precision for throughput (fp8 over bf16 over fp16) or higher precision for accuracy.

Advisor ranking ('NIM automatic selection' goal): exact gpu_device match > GPU-name / compute-capability engine > generic; then NVIDIA-optimized (nim_optimized or prebuilt TensorRT engine), efficient precision, non-LoRA, throughput profile, and the profile that uses the most of the GPUs you gave it.

compatibility_checks.rule: gpu_device is '<pciDeviceId>:<pciVendorId>' (example 2330:10de). Read it on the node with 'lspci -nn | grep -i nvidia' and reverse the bracketed [10de:2330]. A profile with a gpu_device only matches that exact device.
A profile with neither gpu_device nor gpu is GPU-agnostic. A profile that targets a different device is not a match.
Discard a profile when min_vram_per_device_gb is greater than the memory of one GPU (or MIG slice). An absent value means 'unknown', not 'fits'.
required_gpus = tp x pp (absent = 1). Discard the profile when it needs more GPUs than you have (the advisor checks GPUs per node, and number_of_nodes / nnodes for multi-node profiles).
If you need LoRA adapters keep only feat_lora=true profiles (and set NIM_PEFT_SOURCE).

NIM classifies profiles as compatible, low memory (fits only with a shorter context, e.g. --max-model-len 4096) or incompatible. Memory estimates are advisory: a predicted shortfall produces a warning, not a start-up rejection.

Speech, vision and Maxine NIMs often have no gpu_device: they tag TensorRT engines with a list of GPU names plus a compute capability (gpu_cc, compute_capability or gpu_sm_version such as sm_100). The advisor accepts the engine when the GPU is in the name list, or when the GPU has exactly the same compute capability (TensorRT engines are SM-specific; NVIDIA does not guarantee cross-model plans, so this is reported as a warning).
compatibility_checks.source: advisor (observed in nims_catalog/*/model_manifest.yaml, e.g. maxine-bnr, ai4m-relighting, active-speaker-detection-h4m-nim)

compatibility_checks.rule: Some manifests use device_id / gpu_key instead of gpu_device / gpu (llama-3.2-nemoretriever-500m-rerank-v2, paddleocr), write the id without the vendor ('20b2') or in upper case ('2C02'), or pin an SM with gpu_sm_version. The advisor normalizes all of them.

precision_by_architecture.notes: Kernel availability depends on the engine.
T4 (7.5) and V100 (7.0) have no bf16: use fp16 profiles.
precision_by_architecture.source: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm (start-up error 'Bfloat16 is only supported on GPUs with compute capability of at least 8.0')

precision_by_architecture.architectures: Blackwell native; Hopper/Ampere through engine kernels
precision_by_architecture.notes: Used by gpt-oss. Native MXFP4 Tensor Core support is Blackwell only.

precision_by_architecture.architectures: Ada Lovelace (L40S, L4, RTX 6000 Ada), Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell
precision_by_architecture.notes: FP8 W8A8 needs CC >= 8.9. Turing/Ampere can only run FP8 checkpoints as weight-only W8A16 (Marlin), which NIM does not use for profile selection.

precision_by_architecture.architectures: Blackwell: B200/GB200 (10.0), B300/GB300 (10.3), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (12.0), GB10 (12.1)
precision_by_architecture.notes: Fifth-generation Blackwell Tensor Cores. Hopper and older PCAI GPUs (H200 NVL, H100 NVL, L40S) cannot run NVFP4 profiles.

caveats: PCAI 'H200' systems use the PCIe H200 NVL (gpu_device 233b:10de). Many NIMs only ship optimized profiles for the SXM H200 (2335:10de): NIM does not auto-select those on PCAI. Expect a generic vLLM/SGLang profile, or force the SXM profile with NIM_MODEL_PROFILE at your own risk (same GH100 chip and 141 GB).
26b5:10de is the NVIDIA L40. Older LLM NIMs tag profiles 'gpu: L40S' with gpu_device 26b5: NIM will not auto-select them on an L40S (26b9:10de). See the Validation tab.

audio2face-3d tags RTX5080 / RTX5090 / rtx6000-blackwell-sv with 2e01 / 2e02 / 2e14, ids that are not RTX 5080 / 5090 / RTX PRO 6000 in the NVIDIA driver README or pci.ids: those profiles cannot match by gpu_device.
MIG: multi-GPU (tp/pp > 1) profiles cannot span MIG slices, and not every NIM supports MIG instances. Pick the MIG size in the form to check memory fit per slice.
PCAI multi-node inference (AIE 2026.07.1) is an MLIS feature that requires the vLLM model format (Guides/PCAI_docs/PCAI_2026.07.1/12_Data-Science.md:3344-3440).
Profiles and ids change between NIM releases: always confirm with 'list-model-profiles' on the target image before pinning NIM_MODEL_PROFILE.
